scope: C++/Python read-only histogram worker jobs on the shared JobScheduler, with metadata-only resource admission, progress, cancellation, caller-thread completion and detached retained results.
semantics: Commands/limits/options are frozen at submission. The typed job forces source owner tagging and retained-result accounting; an empty supersession key allows independent jobs and explicit keys supersede within the owner. Work runs in C++ using scheduler checkpoints and native histogram accumulation. READY results retain no source/provider handle. Source membership/active/revision checks and atomic UI/preferences/file publication remain the caller responsibility; the job performs no automatic owner edits.
resources: Typed holders and option strings augment the command working estimate. The scheduler reserves max(native estimate, caller resource_bytes). C++ immutable result aliases retain the whole conservative reservation through cancellation/completion/job destruction/shutdown; releasing final aliases wakes queued work. Python results/publication arguments are detached owning copies outside native reservations. Source/cache, opaque provider/publication internals, allocator/scheduler bookkeeping, frontend copies, CSV and RSS are external.
python_publication: Completion invokes Python only on the caller thread. Its callback receives an owning result copy; cancellation loses after Publishing begins. A callback error fails the job and releases its native cell. The original Python exception is rethrown to that caller; persistent scheduler failure state holds a plain native diagnostic rather than Python traceback objects. A weak-reference test proves callback-captured objects can retire after the handled exception.
verification: 581 selected checks per OS including 25 new worker checks, eight native executable suites and fresh installed core-only SDK consumers. Native gates cover queued/running cancellation, immediate last-handle capture release, supersession/document cancellation, detached source lifetime, lease-held queue admission/wakeup, publication/cancellation serialization, callback failures and repeated concurrent result/cancel races. Quiet-NaN payload bits, independent pooled ROI count/statistic expectations, native shared scheduler regressions and prior histogram UI API behavior remain checked. Render-enabled final runs have no skips. No full upstream/resource/platform acceptance.
